title: Rapid Access Evidence Collector and SIEM Schema
body:
Purpose:
This runbook describes a focused evidence-capture and packaging flow for emergency credential access ("break-glass") incidents plus the SIEM export/audit-log schema mappings we use to reconstruct and prove access timelines. It is intended for on-call SREs, security engineers, and incident responders who must rapidly preserve ephemeral credentials and produce an auditable bundle for post-incident review and compliance.

Scope:
- Break-glass/Vault emergency access events (human and automation).
- RBAC v2 role escalation and temporary grants.
- Rotation and revocation steps for compromised secrets.
- SIEM/ELK/Datadog export schema used for evidence ingestion.
- Packaging artifacts and retention for e-discovery.

Quick summary checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Triage and tag incident: create Jira ticket (SEC-xxxx) and set priority.
2) Capture current break-glass grant: run `redwood-identity audit --subject <user-or-service> --since "-1h" --format json > audit-subject.json`.
3) Snapshot live Vault leases and tokens: `vault list auth/token/accessors | xargs -I{} vault read auth/token/lookup-accessor -format=json {} > token-lookup-<ts>.json` (see automation below).
4) Freeze questionable credentials: place immediate TTL=0 hold via the rotator service (`cred-rotator freeze --id <cred-id>`).
5) Notify legal/compliance + on-call sec engineer.
6) Start evidence collector script (below) to stream logs to secure bucket.

RBAC v2 considerations and immediate checks:
- Identify the escalation path: check assignment history for the user/service in RBAC v2 change log: `rbacctl history --principal <id> --since 24h`
- If temporary role grant exists (duration < 7d), record grant id and policy diff. Save `rbac-grant-<id>.json`.
- If grant was via a canary/approval workflow, capture approval chain (Slack thread urls, approval ticket ids).
- Determine if grant was timeboxed or indefinite; if indefinite, escalate to secure revoke immediately.

Evidence collector (manual/one-shot)
- Use the internal collector script `sec-evidence-collector` (packaged in /tools/sec):
  sec-evidence-collector \  \
    --ticket SEC-xxxx \
    --principals "user:alice,service:billing-sync" \
    --since "2025-02-11T09:00:00Z" \
    --target s3://redwood-sec-evidence/SEC-xxxx/\n    --include vault,rbac,audit,edge-logs \
    --encrypt-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/sec-collector

- Output: `evidence-bundle-SEC-xxxx-<ts>.tar.gz` and a metadata file `evidence-manifest.json` that references each artifact and the sha256 checksums.

What to capture (minimum required):
- Vault: token lookup outputs, lease lists, audit device logs for the relevant mount path, and the latest operator actions (creation/revoke/rotate).
- RBAC v2: grant records, policy diffs, principal bindings, and change tickets.
- Audit logs: Redcloak/audit logs (internal), Kubernetes audit events for relevant namespaces, gateway edge-proxy logs (request ids), and API access logs tied to token or principal id.
- SIEM exports: Raw events (JSON) that contain the fields listed in the SIEM schema below.
- Forensics: host snapshots (if credential used on specific host), process lists, and container runtime events (k8s pod, container id).

Immediate revocation and rotation steps:
- For user or machine tokens: `vault token-revoke -accessor <accessor>` and confirm via `vault token-lookup --accessor <accessor>` returns 400/404.
- For service credentials managed by the rotator: run `cred-rotator rotate --id <cred-id> --force --ticket SEC-xxxx` and monitor rotation logs.
- For AWS/Cloud keys: disable IAM key (console or `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id KEY --status Inactive`), then create replacement and apply new key to deployments using staged rollout.
- Post-rotation tests: smoke calls for impacted services and recording of the success/failure trace ids.

SIEM export / Audit log schema (canonical):
We standardize a minimal set of fields to make events queryable for evidence and compliance. Exports must be UTF-8 JSON lines with these top-level fields (all lowercase):
- event_id: string (uuid v4)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (2025-02-11T09:01:23.123Z)
- event_type: string (vault.token.lookup | rbac.grant | cred.rotate | api.request | k8s.exec | login)
- principal_id: string (user:alice | service:billing-sync)
- principal_type: string (user|service|machine)
- actor_ip: string (client ip)
- resource: string (vault/path | iam/key | k8s/pod/name)
- action: string (revoke|create|lookup|login|rotate|approve)
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial)
- trace_id: string (correlates across systems)
- grant_id: string (when event_type relates to rbac.grant)
- authorization_context: string (policy name or scope)
- raw_payload: string (base64 compressed original event payload)
- ingest_source: string (vault-auditd | rbac-v2 | edge-proxy | k8s-audit)
- retention_class: string (A|B|C)  <-- maps to retention policy for legal holds

- Example event (one line valid JSON):
{"event_id":"1e3a6f4a-...","timestamp":"2025-02-11T09:01:23.123Z","event_type":"vault.token.lookup","principal_id":"user:alice","principal_type":"user","actor_ip":"18.205.1.12","resource":"auth/token/lookup","action":"lookup","outcome":"success","trace_id":"trace-7b4","grant_id":"","authorization_context":"admin-policy","raw_payload":"H4sIAAAAA...","ingest_source":"vault-auditd","retention_class":"A"}

SIEM mapping guidance per destination:
- Splunk: send as json_event with sourcetype=redwood:security:audit; index=security-audit. Set _time from timestamp and event_id -> id.
- Elastic: use ecs-compatible mappings. Map event.timestamp, user.id -> principal_id, and put raw_payload in event.original (base64). Tag docs with "retention_class" for ILM lifecycle rules.
- Datadog: use logs API; attach tags:principal:<id>,event_type:<type>,retention:<class> and a facet on grant_id and trace_id for fast queries.

Automation hooks (evidence automation):
- When `rbacctl` issues a temporary grant, it should emit a webhook to `/hooks/sec-evidence` with the full grant payload. The webhook handler will stash the event in the SEC evidence bucket with immediate server-side encryption.
- Vault auditd -> fluentbit -> secure-s3 pipeline must preserve raw bytes. Do not apply parsing transforms before archiving.
- Rotator service must write rotation events to the canonical audit queue and include trace_id and ticket ref.
- A Lambda (or k8s cronjob) will run hourly to re-check open SEC tickets and trigger a reconciliation between recorded grants and actual bindings; discrepancies spawn SEC reconcile tickets.

Retention and legal hold:
- Default retention class mapping: A = 7 years (security evidence), B = 1 year (operational logs), C = 90 days (debug).
- Legal hold supersedes retention; manifest files must flag `legal_hold: true` when triggered and write-hold-to-kms key.

Packaging and handoff for audits:
- Produce a signed tarball with manifest and checksums. Include: evidence-bundle-SEC-xxxx-<ts>.tar.gz, evidence-manifest.json, chain-of-custody.txt (who touched artifacts and when), and redaction notes if PII exists.
- Forensic team to validate SHA256 checksums and sign off. Upload to long-term secure archive with access TTLs configured (grant minimum-privilege access).

Post-incident playbacks and lessons learned:
- Run `sec-playback` to recreate timeline from SIEM and audit artifacts: `sec-playback --bundle evidence-bundle-SEC-xxxx-<ts>.tar.gz --out timeline.md`
- Timeline should map trace ids to human-readable actions, services, and outcomes. Pull in approval threads and the RBAC grant diff.
- Add a short remediation plan (rotate all linked secrets, audit similar grants in last 90 days).

Appendix: common commands / helpers
- Snapshot RBAC grants near a timestamp: `rbacctl list --changed-before "2025-02-11T09:15:00Z" --changed-after "2025-02-11T08:45:00Z" --json > rbac-window.json`
- Vault audit fetch for path: `vault read -format=json sys/audit?path=secret/data/myapp | jq -c .`
- Token accessor extraction helper (quick): `vault token-create -policy=\"emergency\" -orphan -ttl=1h | tee token-out.txt` then immediately stash token-out.txt into evidence.

Notes and open questions:
- Need a canonical mapping from RBAC v2 policy names to authorization_context labels used in SIEM. (OWNER: product-security)
- Consider a hardened ephemeral-storage mode for evidence collector where artifacts are written to encrypted ram-disk before upload (investigate performance and cost).
- Validate that fluentbit pipeline preserves `raw_payload` compression for large payloads (esp. vault audit payloads).

Revision history:
- 2024-07-18: initial draft (Ava Martinez)
- 2024-10-02: added SIEM mapping guidance and Splunk example (Ravi Patel)
- 2025-02-11: clarified retention classes and packaging checklist (Morgan Chu)

End of document.
